evidence.excerpt: High-density board-to-board connectors with pitches below 0.5 mm are difficult to access with flying-probe or bed-of-nails fixtures, making boundary-scan the only practical interconnect verification method. This work describes an algorithm that automatically generates optimised JTAG test vectors for connector nets by traversing the board netlist graph and selecting driver–receiver pairs that maximise fault coverage while minimising vector length. The algorithm was implemented in Python 3.8 and validated on four industrial backplane designs containing between 800 and 2400 connector pins. Generated vector sets achieved 97.3 % stuck-at coverage on average, compared to 89.1 % for vendor-supplied default vectors, while reducing vector count by 31 %. Runtime on a standard workstation was under 90 seconds for the largest design. The tool outputs vectors compatible with the SVF and STAPL formats used by common boundary-scan controllers.
